note: Wipro fact base as of 30-Sep-2026 (Q1FY27 basis). Rupee figures in Rs crore unless stated; IFRS figures from company releases are converted from Rs million. Every item carries src and published. Nothing published after 30-Sep-2026 is used (later facts only in updates/later-facts.json).
segmentsDesc: Two reported segments: IT Services (99%+ of revenue; four Strategic Market Units: Americas 1 = US/LatAm/Canada communications, media, technology, health and consumer; Americas 2 = US/LatAm/Canada banking, capital markets, insurance, energy, manufacturing and resources; Europe = UK & Ireland, Switzerland, Germany, Western Europe; APMEA = Australia/NZ, South-East Asia, Japan, India, Middle East, Africa) and IT Products (resale of security, packaged and SaaS software; Rs 694 cr in FY26). Sectors: BFSI, Consumer, Technology & Communications, Energy/Manufacturing/Resources (EMR), Health. Capco (BFSI consulting) is a business unit. From 1-Apr-2026 LatAm and Canada clients were realigned into Americas 1/2 by sector (history restated). The India state-run enterprise business is no longer reported separately (inside IT Services since FY22).

q2Guide.includes: Mindsprint for the full quarter (two months in Q1)

callPoints: Margin fell 120 bp YoY to 16.0% on the March 2026 salary increase, ramp-up costs of large deals won earlier, AI investments (new AI-native business and platforms unit) and acquisitions moving into execution, partly offset by rupee depreciation (CFO). Management wants to return to its 17-17.5% band but gave no timeline (CEO).
Americas soft: Americas 1 flat YoY, Americas 2 -7.3% YoY (BFSI ramp-up delays, a client-specific issue that ended in Q1, EMR -8.9%). Europe +6% and APMEA +13.5% YoY (BFSI ramps, Mindsprint).
Headcount rose with Mindsprint; excluding it headcount fell by ~2,500 in the quarter. Utilisation 83.6%.

Bookings $3.4 bn with 13 large deals ($1.6 bn); some decisions slipped into Q2. Clients' traditional IT, BPO and support budgets are 'getting compressed' as AI reshapes spending; large cost-takeout deals carry forward productivity and margin pressure; new 'Reimagine AI' work (AI advisory, data priming, agent management, sovereign AI, AI data centres) earns better margins (CEO, CFO).
Gross cash and investments $4.3 bn after the buyback; India investment yield 7.2%; ETR 22.6%. Interim dividend Rs 2; more than $3 bn returned to shareholders in the last year including this dividend.
Wipro guides only one quarter ahead: Q2FY27 -1.5% to +0.5% QoQ in constant currency ($2,574-2,627 mn), which includes a full quarter of Mindsprint.

points: Salary increases effective 1-Mar-2026 (two more months of impact in Q1FY27). DTS (Harman) acquisition fully in Q4 numbers; it and new large deals carry lower margins at first (CFO).
Americas 2 BFSI hit by delayed ramp-ups of large deals and a client-specific issue expected to end in Q1FY27 (CEO).

Olam Group strategic deal expected to exceed $1 bn of contract value with $800 mn committed spend, including the acquisition of Mindsprint (Olam's IT arm); a second vendor-consolidation deal at a top client. Both assumed to contribute 1.5 months in Q1 (~0.7-0.8% of revenue).
Board approved a Rs 15,000 cr buyback at Rs 250 a share (5.7% of equity), the largest in Wipro's history; payout over the three years to FY26 ~88% vs the 70% policy floor.
New AI-native business and platforms unit with dedicated leadership and investment: 'services-as-software' (CEO).
